cover.kicker: Larchmere Trust · Annual review for the family council
cover.title: The year in review, and two decisions for the council
cover.sub: Twelve months to the end of September, net of all fees, against the policy the council set.
cover.meta: October 2026 · Fictional family trust and figures, theme specimen

exec.title: The trust earned {ret}% after fees, ahead of its policy benchmark, and needs one rebalance

rows.p: A strong year for listed equities left them {mv} pp above target and fixed income {fiu} pp below its target. Both remain inside their ranges.
Move ${reb}M from global equities to fixed income, and approve a new private equity commitment to replace the fund now returning capital.

exec.source: Source: Larchmere Trust custodian statements and manager reports (fictional)

chart.title: Global equities earned {rt0}% and drove most of the year's gain

exhibit.title: Net return by asset class, twelve months to 30 September 2026

bullets: Every asset class beat cash except cash itself.
Private equity returned {rt1}% and paid out ${dist}M in distributions.
Fixed income lagged as rates stayed high, but held its value.
takeaway.sowhat: The year rewarded staying invested; it also pushed equities past their target.

chart.source: Source: manager reports and custodian valuations (fictional)
chart.note: Private equity and real assets valued at the latest manager marks, lagged one quarter.

table.title: Equities sit {mv} pp over target and fixed income {fiu} pp under, so we propose a ${reb}M rebalance

exhibit.title: Allocation against the council's policy, 30 September 2026

table.source: Source: custodian statements (fictional); investment policy statement as approved by the council
table.callout: Moving ${reb}M from global equities to fixed income brings both back to target. Doing nothing leaves the trust {mv} pp heavier in equities than the policy the council approved.
table.note: Status: within range when actual is less than 2.5 pp from target; rebalance when further away, even inside the range.
